task.title: Quotation marks
task.shortdesc: Each language has its own quotation marks. CSSMedia writes the marks of the language of the text when you generate quotes with open-quote and close-quote.

context.p: The element name q in the examples is a placeholder. Use the name of the elements that hold quotations in your XML.

info.p: Your XML does not have the quotation marks as text. Generate them with the content property of the pseudo-elements ::before and ::after:
A q inside another q gets the marks of the next level. For English, the outer quotes are “ ” and the inner quotes are ‘ ’. German text gets „ “ and ‚ ‘, and Japanese text gets 「 」.

The quotes property has the initial value auto, which uses the marks of the language. To use other marks, write pairs of strings. The first pair is for the outer level, the second pair for the next level, and so on. The last pair is used for the deeper levels. The value none writes no marks, and match-parent uses the marks of the parent element:
